scenarios.name: AsyncLocalStorage-Glue-Preflight-UNSEALED
scenarios.checks: UNSEALED dry-run before the sealed matrix: CONCURRENCY=2 race with distinct purchase_ids — each slot carried its OWN (owner, purchase_id) into the candidate's evaluate() under the race (adapter-side cross-check adapter_owners_ok=true: both evaluates seen by the pinned Gateway match the per-slot intent, count equality holds); signer=2, deltas 15 ms, both calls before any slot completed; harness-glue validation only, not a matrix row

scenarios.name: IdenticalOfferRace-SharedOwner-Dedup
scenarios.checks: Identical concurrent offers (requirement-amounts 10000,10000), same owner string, same purchase_id, one Gateway: exactly ONE signed payment per mode (signer=1, committed=1); the concurrent duplicate is rejected PRE-SIGNER at the candidate's idempotency layer, verbatim: 'Boundra DENY: within policy — auto-approved; purchase_id already reserved; duplicate signing permission denied' (duplicate=true, purchase_id_conflict=false); rejected slot carries presign_decide=rejected + slot_error and ZERO signer calls (attribution check consistent in both modes); SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes the reservation write so the first-arriving evaluate wins and the second never reaches the signer

scenarios.name: SeparateOwners-SamePurchaseId-NegativeControl
scenarios.checks: Boundary negative control, both modes: DISTINCT owner strings with the SAME purchase_id through ONE Gateway — UNIQUE(owner, purchase_id) does not collide across owners: signer=2, committed=2, zero rejections, behavior unchanged (deltas 9/10 ms). Scope note per pre-registration: owner model = distinct owner STRINGS through one Gateway instance; cross-process without a shared owner is out of scope (recorded, not tested)

scenarios.name: DistinctPurchases-IdenticalQuote
scenarios.checks: Different purchase_ids over an IDENTICAL quote (10000,10000), shared owner, both modes: reservations independent — signer=2, committed=2, zero rejections; no over-blocking of legitimate concurrent purchases

scenarios.name: ConflictingOfferRace-ChangedIntent
scenarios.checks: Same purchase_id, CONFLICTING intents (requirement-amounts 10000,100000 — stand serves the raised offer to one slot), race, both modes: exactly 1 commitment + exactly 1 PRE-SIGNER rejection per mode (signer=1 per mode); the conflict is explicit at the candidate's idempotency layer, verbatim: 'Boundra DENY: within policy — auto-approved; purchase_id conflict: the ID is already bound to a different intent' (duplicate=true, purchase_id_conflict=true); 0 additional signatures after the first commitment. Winner-agnostic per pre-registration (matchers never assert WHICH slot won; winning amount + rejection direction recorded verbatim in the event JSONL): A10a — slot1 committed 10000 (slot2 conflict-rejected); A10b — slot2 committed 100000 (slot1 conflict-rejected). Since the candidate client carries no quote-control (addendum R3), this row doubles as the conflicting-offer control C for BOTH modes: 1 commitment + 1 pre-signer rejection holds in both

scenarios.name: ConflictingOffers-DistinctPurchaseIds-Supplementary
scenarios.checks: SUPPLEMENTARY probe with config-dependent expectation (pre-registered): conflicting offers (10000 vs 100000) under DISTINCT purchase_ids — signer=2, committed=2, zero rejections in both modes. Under the candidate's reservation-only configuration this is the CORRECT behavior (independent purchase ids); the baseline quote-control harness would yield signer=1 here — a configuration fact of the SUT boundary, NOT a regression and not comparable to the cycle-1/2/3 baseline rows

findings_summary.title: Configuration facts recorded per pre-registration addendum R3: (a) NO quote-control in the candidate client — setSpendControls(expectedAmount) is NOT configured and the hook is created without expected_amount/expected_recipient in BOTH modes (the candidate's dedup/conflict semantics are expectation-independent: SHA-256 digest over the canonical intent); (b) the onBeforePaymentCreation hook API exists only in @x402/fetch 2.30.0 — stacking the 2.28.0 PR build with 2.30.0 would be the larger deviation, so the whole stack is 2.30.0 and the cycle-1/2/3 baseline (2.28.0 PR build) is NOT byte-comparable on client deps; (c) therefore case4@A10a := A10c-equivalent and case4@A10b := A10d-equivalent (conflicting-offer control), and the A10a/A10b mode labels are retained for topology comparability only — mechanically identical for this candidate, a result divergence BETWEEN modes is an anomaly, not a mode effect (none observed); (d) rejected slots carry zero signer calls by construction (verified per session: signer_call_count == committed slots in all 10 sessions)

Result: the pinned Boundra pre-sign reservation boundary satisfies the pre-registered matrix on ALL rows — identical concurrent offers admit exactly one signature (duplicate DENY, idempotency layer), conflicting offers under one purchase_id admit exactly one commitment + one explicit pre-signer rejection (purchase_id conflict, idempotency layer), separate owners and distinct purchase ids continue to sign independently (no over-blocking). Signer-call deltas 7-16 ms across race sessions (baseline band 7-9 ms). Verdicts are claims about the CANDIDATE's boundary vs the pre-registered matrix, not about the x402 protocol or the #4198 baseline: the baseline client (no reservation layer) still exhibits the F-A10 identical-offer race per argus-seal-0008/0012

notes: First of the two pre-registered candidates of the x402 #4198 identical-offer-race test (order fixed in the issue thread: boundra fb09284 -> gist df69c25; the second run drafts as record 0019). Evidence discipline: signer-boundary observability (presign_decide=rejected + slot_error, signer untouched) or signing (signer_call); NO on-chain transfer established (settlement mocked); no private keys, no signatures, no usable authorizations in evidence; session event ledgers + adapter verdict logs + per-session SQLite state exported to attestations/evidence/0018-boundra-a10/ with export-hashes.json.
